decisions.reason: As a newly launched extension of the firm's core coolant-management business, with visible market introduction and likely engineering investment already committed, management would be inclined to continue backing it.

This centrifuge fits the firm's established filtration and process-media offering, so a large German machinery producer with in-house R&D would likely justify staying the course rather than reversing after only one year.
Although coolant nozzles may be easier to prune than larger systems, they still complement the firm's core solution portfolio and public launch commitment makes an early withdrawal unlikely.

The scraper belt chip conveyor is close to the firm's existing material-flow offer, and management following escalation-of-commitment logic would tend to attribute any early weakness to market ramp-up rather than drop it quickly.

Because the magnetic belt chip conveyor builds directly on an established product family and supports the firm's stated growth in smarter production solutions, management would be disposed to retain it.

Even if the hinged belt chip conveyor is somewhat easier to discontinue than more central platform products, the firm has already invested in launch, range breadth and customer signaling, which favors keeping it on the market.
